Key quantities  
1. Distance from the Large Magellanic Cloud to Earth: about 160 000–165 000 light-years.  
   (Use 160 000 ly for a round figure.)  
2. Ship’s speed: v = 0.999 999 87 c.

Step 1: Lorentz factor γ  
Let ε = 1 – v/c = 1.3 × 10⁻⁷.  
Then 1 – v²/c² ≃ 2ε ≈ 2.6 × 10⁻⁷.  
γ = 1/√(1 – v²/c²) ≈ 1/√(2.6 × 10⁻⁷) ≈ 1/0.000509 9 ≈ 1.96 × 10³ ≈ 1960.

Step 2: Time in the Earth frame  
t_Earth = (distance)/(speed) ≈ 160 000 ly / 0.999 999 87 ≈ 160 000 yr.

Step 3: Proper time experienced by the astronaut  
τ = t_Earth / γ ≈ 160 000 yr / 1960 ≈ 81.6 yr.

Thus the 22-year-old astronaut would experience about 82 years in transit and arrive roughly aged 104, well within the 150-year life expectancy.

The closest listed choice is 81 years.

Answer: A
